gaps.sentence: Hamlet ___ (perform) almost continuously since it was written.
gaps.explanation: 'Since + past clause' requires present perfect passive: has been + performed.

gaps.sentence: This machine ___ (NOT USE) for years before I repaired it.
gaps.hint: negative passive before a past point
gaps.explanation: The disuse continued up to the past repair: past perfect passive hadn't been used.

gaps.sentence: My laptop ___ (service) next week, so back up your files beforehand.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' takes the future passive: will be + serviced (is being serviced is also a valid arrangement).

gaps.sentence: You should get that rash ___ (look at) by a doctor.
gaps.explanation: Causative 'get something done': get + object + past participle (looked at).

gaps.sentence: The decision ___ (announce) at yesterday's press conference.
gaps.explanation: 'Yesterday' signals past simple passive: was + announced.

gaps.sentence: The new bridge ___ (open) by the mayor next month.
gaps.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + opened, with the agent in a by-phrase.

gaps.sentence: The theatre ___ in 1897 and reopened last year.
gaps.explanation: A finished date (1897) takes past simple passive: was + built.

gaps.sentence: The stage was still wet — the scenery ___ (paint) only hours before.
gaps.explanation: 'Only hours before' points to the past perfect passive: had been + painted.
